The destroy retained-resource predicate previously used `jsonb_array_elements_text(...) address where address=r.address`. PostgreSQL's named output column is `value`; column resolution finds the correlated outer `r.address` before a whole-row alias. That excluded all retained rows when the base-address list was nonempty. An explicit `base_address(value)` alias and qualified `base_address.value=r.address` preserve the complete native retained set. Primary source references are PostgreSQL 16's [JSON function catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_16_STABLE/src/include/catalog/pg_proc.dat), [function alias resolution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_16_STABLE/src/backend/parser/parse_relation.c) and [column reference resolution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_16_STABLE/src/backend/parser/parse_expr.c). Root's separate real PostgreSQL scalar probe confirmed the old predicate excludes a retained row and the corrected predicate retains it; this author performed no database execution.
